chunks: Those who trade on the promises of God, and who purchase a little gain from their oaths, will have no share in the life to come. God will not address or even regard them on the Day of Resurrection, nor perfect them, and their suffering will be painful.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to trade God's covenant for a small price?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the breach of the Covenant of Alast or specific political covenants by the elite, highlighting the gravity of trading divine promises for transient worldly gain. The triad of deprivation—God not speaking to them, not looking at them, and not purifying them—signifies a complete severance from divine grace and spiritual cleanliness. This serves as a stern warning against hypocrisy and the commodification of faith for political or material advantage.
